examples.ko: 그 동굴은 아주 깊숙해서 불빛이 안 닿아요.
examples.en: That cave is so deep that light doesn't reach it.

examples.ko: 서랍이 깊숙해서 물건이 잘 안 보여요.
examples.en: The drawer is deep, so I can't see things well.

examples.ko: 깊숙한 골목 안에 작은 카페가 있어요.
examples.en: There is a small cafe deep inside the alley.

examples.ko: 반지는 가방 깊숙한 곳에 넣어 뒀어요.
examples.en: I put the ring deep inside my bag.
The deeper into the forest you go, the quieter it gets.

examples.ko: 산속 깊숙한 곳에 있던 그 절은 찾기 힘들었어요.
examples.en: That temple tucked deep in the mountains was hard to find.

explain: '깊다'는 위에서 아래로 깊이를 말하고, '깊숙하다'는 바깥에서 안쪽으로 멀리 들어간 곳을 말해요. 그래서 서랍, 가방, 산속, 골목처럼 안으로 들어가는 곳에 어울려요. 보통 '깊숙한 곳', '깊숙이'로 써요.
explain_en: 깊다 describes depth from top to bottom, while 깊숙하다 describes a spot that is far inside from the outside. That is why it suits drawers, bags, mountains and alleys. It usually appears as 깊숙한 곳 or 깊숙이.

examples.en: This bag is fine even in the rain.
I'm fine even if I stay up all night.
They say it's a sturdy building, so it won't budge even in an earthquake.

examples.ko: 감기에 걸린 친구들과 있어도 저는 끄떡없었어요.
examples.en: Even around friends with colds, I stayed perfectly fine.

examples.ko: 아무리 힘든 일이 닥쳐도 그는 끄떡없어 보여요.
examples.en: No matter how hard things get, he looks unshaken.
Will this phone be okay even if I drop it?

explain: 어떤 충격이나 힘든 일이 있어도 흔들리거나 상하지 않고 멀쩡한 상태를 말해요. 사람과 물건 모두에 쓰고, 보통 '~에도 끄떡없다', '~도 끄떡없다'로 말해요. 비슷한 '멀쩡하다'는 다치거나 고장 나지 않은 상태 자체를 말해요.
explain_en: It describes staying unshaken and undamaged even when facing a shock or hardship. It is used for both people and things, usually as '~에도 끄떡없다' or '~도 끄떡없다'. The similar '멀쩡하다' focuses on simply being uninjured or not broken.

examples.ko: 길이 부드러운 반원을 그리며 휘어 있어요.
examples.en: The road curves in a gentle semicircle.
The students sat in a semicircle in front of the teacher.
Try drawing a semicircle with a compass.

examples.ko: 다리 아래로 반원 모양의 터널이 보여요.
examples.en: I can see a semicircle-shaped tunnel under the bridge.
I cut the cake into a half-circle shape.
The diameter of a semicircle is the same as that of the circle.

explain: 원을 반으로 나눈 모양이에요. 의자 배치나 도형 문제에 자주 나와요. 모양을 말할 때는 '반달 모양'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the shape you get when you cut a circle in half. It often comes up in seating arrangements and geometry problems. For the shape, people also say '반달 모양' (half-moon shape).

examples.en: It's a sheer curtain, so some light comes in.

examples.ko: 이 비닐봉지는 반투명해서 안이 흐릿하게 보여요.
examples.en: This plastic bag is translucent, so the inside looks blurry.
The bathroom glass is frosted.
I put the snacks in a translucent plastic container.
I put a translucent film on the new window.
The ice turned translucent as it melted.

explain: '투명'은 뒤까지 다 보이고, '반투명'은 빛은 통하지만 모양이 흐릿하게 보여요. 반대말은 '불투명'이에요. '반투명 유리'처럼 다른 말 앞에 붙이거나 '반투명하다'로 써요.
explain_en: '투명' lets you see through completely, while '반투명' lets light through but the shapes look blurry. The opposite is '불투명'. It is used before another noun, as in '반투명 유리', or as '반투명하다'.

examples.en: This watch is a little inaccurate with the time.
You shouldn't trust inaccurate information.

examples.ko: 그 기사는 내용이 부정확해서 다시 고쳤어요.
examples.en: The article's content was inaccurate, so it was corrected.
Isn't my pronunciation imprecise?

examples.ko: 부정확하게 말하면 오해가 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you speak imprecisely, misunderstandings can arise.
The map must have been inaccurate, because I got lost.

explain: 반대말은 '정확하다'예요. '정확하지 않다'라고 풀어서 말해도 같은 뜻이에요. '틀리다'는 아예 맞지 않다는 뜻이라서, 대체로 맞지만 어딘가 모자랄 때는 '부정확하다'를 써요.
explain_en: The opposite is '정확하다', and '정확하지 않다' says the same thing in two words. '틀리다' means completely wrong, so for something that is mostly right but not exact, use '부정확하다'.

examples.ko: 하늘이 잿빛으로 흐려서 곧 비가 올 것 같아요.
examples.en: The sky is clouded in ash-gray, so it looks like rain soon.
Gray clouds hang low.
The winter sea is gray, so it looks lonely.
Grandfather's hair has turned ash-gray before I knew it.
Wearing a gray coat makes me look calm.
That dog's fur is close to ash-gray.

explain: 검은색이 아니라 재처럼 탁한 회색이에요. 하늘, 구름, 바다, 도시처럼 흐리고 쓸쓸한 분위기에 자주 쓰고, 일반적인 색 이름은 '회색'이에요. 발음은 [재삗]이에요.

phrases.en: The economy is bad, so next year's outlook is bleak.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞날이 밝지 않고 어둡다는 비유로 뉴스나 글에서 쓰여요.
phrases.nuance_en: A figurative way to say the future looks dim, used in news and writing.

explain_en: It is a dull ash gray, not black. It is often used for gloomy scenes like skies, clouds, seas and cities, while the everyday color name is '회색'. It is pronounced [재삗].

examples.en: If you leave clothes in the washer too long, they get wrinkly.
Grandma's hands are wrinkled, but they are warm.
I flattened the crumpled paper with an iron.
The apple is old, so its skin has shriveled.
I was in the water so long that my fingers are wrinkly.
I threw away the tangerine that had dried up and shriveled.

explain: 마르거나 오그라들어서 주름이 많이 진 모양에 써요. 옷이나 종이가 구겨진 건 '구깃구깃하다'나 '구겨지다'라고도 해요. 사람 피부에는 '주름이 많다'고 말하는 쪽이 부드러워요.
explain_en: It describes something with many wrinkles because it dried out or shrank. For crumpled clothes or paper, people also say '구깃구깃하다' or '구겨지다'. For a person's skin, saying '주름이 많다' sounds gentler.
